The closest match is Raven, a linear-time sequence model for long-context recall that uses fixed memory slots and learned input-dependent routing to reduce interference and hard eviction, improving long-range content recovery over prior linear-time baselines [1]. It is described as competitive with or better than prior linear-time models on recall-intensive benchmarks and effective when extrapolating to context lengths up to 16x training length [1].

If you want other linear-time recall methods, Kaczmarz Linear Attention improves retrieval in a linear recurrent model and reaches 100% on single-needle retrieval, while Adaptive Memory Decay for Log-Linear Attention learns input-dependent decay and improves associative recall and selective copying [2, 3].
